label: The evening of the race, in a Pullman car back to London
quote: We had the corner of a Pullman car to ourselves that evening as we whirled back to London
note: Holmes tells Colonel Ross and Watson what happened on the Monday night and how he worked it out (¶215–231). This is the 'more fitting time' he promised (¶214).
This was planned at ¶214. It comes about in the Pullman car that evening (t.pullman, ¶215). The next race, on which Holmes has a bet, comes in between.

label: Monday, when curried mutton was chosen for supper at the trainer's house
quote: the only two people who could have chosen curried mutton for supper that night
note: Holmes's reasoning. Only Straker or his wife could have chosen the dish.

label: Monday evening, when the stable-lad's dish was set aside
quote: The opium was added after the dish was set aside for the stable-boy

label: Monday evening, when the opium was added to the stable-lad's dish
quote: The opium was added after the dish was set aside for the stable-boy
note: This comes before the maid carries the supper down. Holmes asks who had access to the dish without the maid seeing them.

label: Monday evening, the same dish eaten at the house
quote: for the others had the same for supper with no ill effects

label: Monday evening, when Fitzroy Simpson dropped his cravat in his flight
quote: Simpson in his flight had dropped his cravat
note: Holmes's account. This contradicts Simpson's claim that he had lost it (t.simpson_lost_cravat).

label: Monday night, when Straker picked up the cravat
note: Holmes says 'perhaps' it was to secure the horse's leg. The text does not say where or exactly when Straker picked it up.

Holmes says Straker went down to the stables in the dead of the night and took out Silver Blaze (¶220). The dog did not bark enough to wake the lads (¶219). The police had held that Simpson took him out (¶46).
This is the night of the crime, when the horse was fetched out of the stable and the dog did not bark enough to wake the two lads (¶219).

label: Monday night, Straker leads the horse out to the hollow
quote: Straker had led out the horse to a hollow where his light would be invisible

note: Holmes says Straker had taken off his overcoat, in spite of the rain, in order to do his delicate task (¶226). There was no wind but very heavy rain (¶94–95). The coat was later seen from the knoll (¶35).
Holmes says Straker got behind the horse and struck a light just before the horse lashed out (¶226). The Colonel says this is why he struck the match (¶224).

This is the struggle in the hollow on Monday night (¶19, ¶35–37), after Straker left the house at one and before seven in the morning. Holmes says the horse was frightened by the light and lashed out, and the steel shoe struck Straker on the forehead. As he fell, his own knife gashed his thigh (¶226).

label: Monday night, when the horse bolted
quote: Ah, it bolted, and was cared for by one of your neighbours

label: Before the crime, when Straker practised the tendon-nicking on the sheep
quote: so astute a man as Straker would not undertake this delicate tendon-nicking without a little practice
note: Holmes's surmise, which he says the lad's answer confirmed. This is what lamed the three sheep.

label: Cases before now, when trainers laid against their own horses and stopped them by fraud
quote: There have been cases before now where trainers have made sure of great sums of money by laying against their own horses
note: This is a general past and is not dated.

label: The time when Straker led a double life as Derbyshire, with a second establishment
quote: Straker was leading a double life, and keeping a second establishment
note: The milliner knew him as an excellent customer named Derbyshire, with a very dashing wife (¶229). Holmes believes she plunged him into debt. This period takes in the milliner's account (t.milliner_account) and the letters addressed to Derbyshire (t.derbyshire_letters).

label: When Holmes, back in London, called upon the milliner
quote: When I returned to London I called upon the milliner
note: Holmes takes Straker's photograph with him (¶225). The text does not order this against the train to Winchester.

label: The evening of the race, passing Clapham Junction
quote: This is Clapham Junction, if I am not mistaken

label: The evening of the race, at Victoria, in less than ten minutes
quote: we shall be in Victoria in less than ten minutes

label: The evening of the race, a cigar in Holmes and Watson's rooms
quote: If you care to smoke a cigar in our rooms, Colonel
note: Holmes offers this to the Colonel.
